pr_comments:
@oniko this touches some of the code you added. ptal!

(BTW, @oniko: i am wondering, what's the rationale for going through the token plugins from systemd-cryptsetup? I mean, we implement the non-plugin codepaths anyway, hence what do we gain in systemd-cryptsetup to go via the plugins for that? I am tempted to drop those codepaths, and not bother for the token modules that are anyway implemented in systemd code. My reason for that: I'd like to rework the FIDO2 stuff so that we can ask the same question to multiple enrolled tokens, and then depending on the answer we get check if any of the enrolled ones match. But that means we want to reuse data we acquired from one token possibly on the next token and so on. that is easy if we don't bother with the plugins for the fido2 stuff. if we always go via the plugins also for the fido2 stuff passing this data is not as easy. hence my question: can we drop the plugin codepaths from systemd-cryptsetup? what would we lose?)

> Fixes: #10739

Wrong issue number I imagine?

> Wrong issue number I imagine?

Fixed.
LGTM. But Ubuntu CIs are red.

> LGTM. But Ubuntu CIs are red.

There are testbed issues, so we can ignore those. But the new env var could use being documented.
Added a brief explanation of that new env var. Upgrading green label, since this is minor stuff.

> (BTW, @oniko: i am wondering, what's the rationale for going through the token plugins from systemd-cryptsetup? I mean, we implement the non-plugin codepaths anyway, hence what do we gain in systemd-cryptsetup to go via the plugins for that? I am tempted to drop those codepaths, and not bother for the token modules that are anyway implemented in systemd code.

Just to reassure myself. You'd want to drop crypt_activate_by_token* libcryptsetup API usage in systemd-cryptsetup completely?

If so, please consider not doing so. I'll try to explain below:

> My reason for that: I'd like to rework the FIDO2 stuff so that we can ask the same question to multiple enrolled tokens, and then depending on the answer we get check if any of the enrolled ones match. But that means we want to reuse data we acquired from one token possibly on the next token and so on.

Can't you create custom context and pass it via usrptr in crypt_activate_by_token* calls? The internal logic in crypt_activate_by_token* guarantees that if you pass "systemd-fido2" token type as parameter the context (usrptr) gets passed only to systemd-fido2 tokens and you may keep that data there.

> that is easy if we don't bother with the plugins for the fido2 stuff. if we always go via the plugins also for the fido2 stuff passing this data is not as easy. hence my question: can we drop the plugin codepaths from systemd-cryptsetup? what would we lose?)

Frankly? Systemd itself perhaps not so much. But my goal was eliminate as much as possible code duplication in between systemd and cryptsetup. Recall that cryptsetup had it's own tpm2 integration on the table at the moment systemd implemented systemd-tpm2 token and associated logic. And we dropped our implementation in favor of systemd one, so that there was no userbase split.

There are other libcryptsetup internal  things. Libcryptsetup API calls respect keyslot priorities, it can easily see keyslot elligibility for current effective volume key (so you don't waste, just an example, PIN try on a token with unusable keyslot for whatever reason). Then there's reencryption (multiple effective volume keys) and so on.

So, is there anything we can do (on libcryptsetup side, do you miss any particular API) to avoid this? I guess the moment you drop crypt_activate_token* logic from systemd we will (sooner or later) end with systemd tokens being unusable from cryptsetup cli due to some future incompatibility.
@poettering Could you please repond to @oniko comments?

> Can't you create custom context and pass it via usrptr in crypt_activate_by_token* calls? The internal logic in crypt_activate_by_token* guarantees that if you pass "systemd-fido2" token type as parameter the context (usrptr) gets passed only to systemd-fido2 tokens and you may keep that data there.

Sure, it's obviously possible to do things like that, but it's so much easier if we don't have to do it that way ;-)

So, the main reason I was asking was that I dislike the fact that there are currently two quite different codepaths in place that do pretty much the same and we need to support for quite a while I guess. I'd really like to cut down on this, simply because i don#t follow myself anymore which codepath followed for which case anymore.

now there are two options: drop the old non-plugin codepaths or drop the new plugin-based codepath. I sympathize that you'd rather not see the latter go and want to see that tested. I guess getting rid of the old non-plugin codepath is something we can't do so quickly (i.e. we intend to maintain compat for 2y old versions of depending libs usually), that's why i was asking whether we can maybe drop the new-style codepath. 

now i see two avenues to make this more maintainable and still get all the testing we need:

1. drop the new style plugin-based activation in systemd-cryptsetup, and in place beef up our test suite to do more testing of the upstream cryptsetup binary with out plugin, to ensure that whatever systemd-cryptsetup/systemd-cryptenroll does remains usuable with upstream cryptsetup
2. we try to reduce the old codepaths in systemd-cryptsetup, and try to make them work more like the new codepaths. i.e. add some wrapper code somewhere that fakes plugin-like behaviour for old cryptsetup. i.e. some compat func we include in our tree that does something akin to crypt_activate_by_token_pin() but just passes the data directly to out backend if libcryptsetup doesn't support plugins natively. i.e. we'd still pack things up in the `systemd_pkcs11_plugin_params` struct (and similar), and from the main program everything looks roughly the same, even though in one case libcrytsetp dlopens some shared object in the background and in the other case we just dispatch things directly. (in other words, I'd like to reduce HAVE_LIBCRYPTSETUP_PLUGINS ifdeffery in our main programs, and instead move that to some helper glue that simply uses two different paths to path the plugin data along.) 

I guess you'd prefer the 2nd option, and I think I would too, given that the plugins stuff is certainly more future-proof.
Thank you. Option 2) sounds great! Btw we're going to test systemd plugins in cryptsetup testsuite as well. Upstream CI is basically ready but we wait for systemd v250 release.

issue_context.title: cryptsetup: add configurable timeout for waiting for security token insertion during boot
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
It seems that currently there is not simple way to unlock LUKS volume when pkcs11-uri=auto specified in /etc/crypttab for the volume.

It is a painful situation when you lost the security token and need to unlock the root volume on boot.

systemd-cryptsetup displays 'Security token XXX not present for unlocking volume test, please plug it in.' and wait for the token. At least I did not figure out the simple way to skip this request and fallback to the password or keyfile.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Probably systemd-cryptsetup should silently fallback to the password or keyfile authentication method.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Optionally systemd-cryptsetup can fallback the password or keyfile authentication method only if token-timeout (or even just keyfile-timeout) specified.

**The systemd version you checked that didn't have the feature you are asking for**
systemd 248
comments: I think it's the same for fido2-device=auto. Would also like a fallback or even a user choice from all available methods (that have been configured for a slot)

the problem is that during boot hardware pops up continously. i.e. disk drivers show up and we try to activate them, and concurrently hid devices show up. If we'd check for HID/FIDO2/PKCS11 devices only at the moment we try to activate a LUKS device, then this would be very unreliable, since there's a major chance the security device isn't probed yet, but will be instants later.

So, to fix this we actively have to wait for the device to show up.

Now, we certainly should add a timeout for this. I was thinking about adding support for asking for pw and security token insertion simultaneously. But that sucks a bit, since this might mean we might suddenly change the prompt from asking for pw to asking for PIN once the security token is detected.

> Now, we certainly should add a timeout for this. I was thinking about adding support for asking for pw and security token insertion simultaneously. But that sucks a bit, since this might mean we might suddenly change the prompt from asking for pw to asking for PIN once the security token is detected.

How about user choice, i.e. asking the user which (configured) slot they'd want to use?
 This would also provide a workaround for: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/19208

I think it's different enough from the original request here, so I've created a new ticket for my suggestion: #19764 

Of course feel free to close if you disagree with it warranting a separate ticket.
